Immunohistochemistry showed strong positivity for CD31, ERG, and MDM2, while CD34, factor VIII, cytokeratins, and hormone receptors were negative, excluding primary breast carcinoma and supporting the diagnosis of metastatic vascular sarcoma of non-mammary origin (Figure 3). Surgical resection was not pursued because of poor functional status (ECOG performance status 4), extensive local invasion precluding complete resection, and evidence of metastatic disease.
